chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Four [characteristics] in whoever they are found, God will build for him a house in Paradise: whoever shelters the orphan, shows mercy to the weak, is compassionate to his parents, and is kind to his slave.
ai.seo_question: What four characteristics lead to God building a house in Paradise?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS), linking these four specific virtues to the divine promise of a dedicated abode in Paradise, emphasizing the integration of social welfare (orphans, the weak) with familial piety (parents) and domestic ethics (slaves). This narration reflects the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a tangible means of spiritual elevation, where mercy towards dependents is seen as a direct reflection of one's readiness for eternal reward.
